entries.context: The self-improve skill was installed locally but could not run legitimately because the workspace had no codex-setup control plane.
entries.symptom: Stage 0 failed because codex-setup/ and codex-setup/agent-memory/shared/MEMORY.md were missing.
entries.root_cause: The workspace had a local deployed skill in ~/.codex/skills/self-improve but no repo-native Codex source-of-truth, whiteboard, state, or bridge helpers.
entries.verification: Created codex-setup, mirrored the self-improve skill into codex-setup/skills/self-improve, verified whiteboard-bridge print-directive and directive-token, and ran session-start-sync successfully.
entries.portability_notes: Other CLIs should bootstrap their own repo-local control plane before relying on locally deployed skills.
entries.resilience_summary: Added repo-native whiteboard, rules, state files, bridge registry, delta audit stubs, and ledger helper scripts so future runs no longer depend on claude-code-setup or hidden local state.

entries.summary: Hardening for self-improve loader, Windows heredoc guard, and session scorer runtime binding
entries.context: The A1/A2/B1 tranche from the 2026-04-22 self-improve review targeted three recurring environment failures in Codex.
entries.symptom: self-improve could disappear from loader visibility, Bash heredoc Python snippets stayed possible on Windows, and session-scores.jsonl was never produced by the active runtime.
entries.root_cause: The environment lacked a shared validator, the Windows Bash guard did not block Python heredocs, and the active Codex launch path no longer invoked a scorer that understood the current transcript location and schema.
entries.verification: Added the codex-setup validator, deployed the updated self-improve skill, blocked Python heredoc in bash-guard.ps1, rebound the session scorer via the PowerShell profile, manually created ~/.codex/session-scores.jsonl through the scorer, and reached clean validator status.
entries.portability_notes: Other CLIs should keep a repo-native validator plus an active-runtime scorer hook that is tested against the current transcript schema.
entries.resilience_summary: A1 adds loader-safe frontmatter checks, A2 blocks the Windows failure mode before execution, and B1 restores session score generation with a schema-tolerant scorer and active launcher binding.

entries.context: User requested porting Claude Code setup intelligence into codex-setup so Codex can inspect foreign setup deltas without depending on Claude control files.
entries.symptom: codex-setup/scripts/audit-claude-delta.mjs and audit-gemini-delta.mjs were stubs that only reported readiness and could not classify ADD/ADAPT/REPLACE candidates.
entries.root_cause: The initial Codex setup bootstrap created placeholder delta audit scripts but did not port Claude Code's bridge registry helper, real Git delta scanner, bridge metadata, or bootstrap report infrastructure.
entries.verification: node --check passed for bridge-registry.mjs, audit-claude-delta.mjs, audit-gemini-delta.mjs, and bootstrap-report.mjs; JSON bridge files parse; audit-claude-delta scan produces candidates; bootstrap-report emits Codex bridge metadata.
entries.portability_notes: Other CLI setups can copy the pattern: registry helper plus per-peer bridge JSON plus Git-based scanner, with foreign sources read-only and replacement candidates requiring confirmation.
entries.resilience_summary: Defense in depth: bridge registry is machine-readable, audit scripts classify risk, README documents commands, validate-codex-setup now checks bridge infrastructure, and ledgers record the environment fix.

entries.summary: Fix codex-mem worker guard PowerShell Host variable collision
entries.context: User reported a previous CLI crash and asked to continue fixing broken skills and hooks. Hook logs showed repeated codex-mem-worker-guard shim failures on 2026-06-09.
entries.symptom: SessionStart log contained: codex-mem-worker-guard shim failed: Cannot overwrite variable Host because it is read-only or constant.
entries.root_cause: claude-mem-worker-guard.ps1 used a parameter named Host in Test-ServiceHealthy and Patch-PluginHooks. PowerShell reserves System.Management.Automation.Internal.Host.InternalHost as a read-only automatic variable, so binding -Host failed before the worker guard could run.
entries.verification: Parsed ~/.codex/config.toml with tomllib, confirmed all registered hook scripts exist, confirmed no remaining -Host parameter references in active and repo guard scripts, and prepared direct hook execution verification.
entries.portability_notes: PowerShell hook functions must avoid automatic variable names such as Host, Error, PID, HOME, and args. Mirror active hook fixes into codex-setup/hooks so restore/sync does not reintroduce the bug.
entries.resilience_summary: Renamed function parameters to HostName in both active and repo guard scripts, updated call sites, and hardened active hook commands with -NoProfile to reduce profile-output interference.

entries.summary: Fix Windows Codex shell PATH casing for command discovery
entries.context: During the hook and skill recovery run, node, where.exe, and rg were not discoverable by command name even though their directories existed in the process PATH.
entries.symptom: Commands failed with 'The term node/where.exe/rg is not recognized', while explicit paths such as C:/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe worked.
entries.root_cause: ~/.codex/config.toml set shell_environment_policy.set.PATH on Windows. PowerShell command discovery in this Codex-launched process used the canonical Path variable; copying PATH into Path immediately restored node.exe and where.exe resolution.
entries.verification: ~/.codex/config.toml now parses and contains shell_environment_policy.set.Path. In a process where Path was aligned to PATH, node v24.15.0, where.exe, and rg 15.1.0 resolved correctly. Existing running tool processes may need a fresh Codex start to inherit the fixed key.
entries.portability_notes: Windows restore code should write Path, while Unix restore code should keep PATH. The shared Python helper now supports a path key and replaces old casing case-insensitively.
entries.resilience_summary: Updated active config, Windows restore script, and the shared ensure-codex-git-lock-config helper so future restores do not recreate the uppercase-PATH failure mode.

entries.summary: Fix Codex skill frontmatter and active session scorer validation errors
entries.context: The Codex setup validator still reported 13 errors after hook repair during a full skills/hooks recovery run.
entries.symptom: Validator reported long or YAML-fragile local skill descriptions and an active session-scorer.ts that still referenced whiteboard-insert side effects.
entries.root_cause: Several deployed local skills had frontmatter descriptions over the validator limit or inline YAML-fragile ': ' text. The active session-scorer.ts had drifted behind the repo side-effect-free version.
entries.verification: validate-codex-setup.mjs now reports 543 repo skills, 555 local skills, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Select-String confirms the active session-scorer.ts no longer contains whiteboard-insert, Insert-WhiteboardEntry, or insertViaWhiteboardInsert.
entries.portability_notes: Keep Skill descriptions short, one-line, and quoted. Restore scripts must copy repo hook sources to the active runtime so validator state cannot drift.
entries.resilience_summary: Batch-normalized 11 local skill frontmatters, mirrored the four repo-backed skill sources, and redeployed the repo session-scorer.ts to the active hook directory.
